assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a Higgs-like boson at 125 GeV by ATLAS and CMS was the decisive empirical clue from nature for the electroweak sector. Discovery came first and theory second here, which is how I like to see a prize built. Originality lies in the detector concepts and the analysis that turned a rare signal into a firm discovery. The lasting impact is a measured scalar sector that anchors all of particle physics.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theorists but left the experimental discovery unrecognised. The credited names are the founding conceiving figures of the two experiments (Jenni for ATLAS, Della Negra and Virdee for CMS), which gives a workable one-to-three split across both collaborations. The huge collaborations and the many people behind the detectors make any individual choice contestable. I would want the expert reports to confirm that these three are the right proxies.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by two experiments, plus a decade of coupling and spin-parity measurements, makes this very mature. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether naming founding spokespersons fairly represents the decisive contributions inside collaborations of thousands.
I rely on my own knowledge of the roles of these three and have not verified them independently.
Whether the committee wants to honour a collaboration-based discovery again after the 2013 theory prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and later Sgr A* are direct observational evidence of the near-horizon environment of black holes. This is a clue from nature with real existential weight and links to my own interest in horizons and horizonless alternatives. The originality is the VLBI technique at 1.3 mm and the imaging pipeline. The ring size is consistent with general relativity, though it is not a tight test of alternatives.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT effort to realise it and Zensus built the VLBI and institutional base. This is a reasonable trio, but a collaboration of hundreds, with large contributions from imaging and theory teams, makes the allocation open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: M87* was imaged in 2019, the polarisation was measured in 2021 and Sgr A* followed in 2022, with consistent results across epochs. This is quite mature, though still young compared with typical timing. The interpretation of the shadow is stable.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among instrument builders, observers, imaging algorithm developers and theorists is disputed.
How tightly the images constrain horizonless or modified-gravity alternatives is still debated.
Whether the committee sees this as discovery of a new phenomenon or as a technical milestone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the CMB anisotropies into a precision tool and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model, including age, curvature and matter content, with the acoustic peaks as clear clues from nature. Its impact on our picture of the universe has been enormous. The originality is the mission design and the analysis that extracted cosmological parameters.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the principal investigator, Page was a leading instrument and design scientist, and Spergel was a central figure in the analysis and cosmological interpretation. This is a coherent three-person configuration, though others in the WMAP team also made decisive contributions.
assessment.maturity: The results were independently confirmed and refined by Planck, so the interpretation is very stable. Cosmology was recognised in 2006 (COBE), 2011 and 2019, so timing is reasonable, though the novelty has partly been overtaken by Planck.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will see WMAP as sufficiently distinct from COBE and Planck.
Fair credit for the very large WMAP team, in particular Wilkinson, Hinshaw and others, is not covered by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane neutrino signal, opened a new window on the universe. It is a discovery in the plain sense, with obvious interest for the origin of cosmic rays. The originality is the use of a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice as a detector.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the leading conceiver and PI of IceCube, and Spiering was central to the early neutrino telescope projects (AMANDA and Baikal-era work) and the path to IceCube. Two names give a clean configuration, though the AMANDA and Baikal groups and others also contributed.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed at high significance. Source identification is still developing, with only a few candidate sources, so the field is partly young. The case is strong but may be somewhat early for a full sources story.
uncertainties: The sources of most of the flux remain unidentified.
The role of Baikal and other early pioneers could complicate the allocation of credit.
Whether the prize is better held until the source population is clearer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a new class of matter and a new organising principle. The theory was tied quickly to measurement, which suits my emphasis on confirmation by nature. The impact on condensed matter has been broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposals, and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicting HgTe. The supplied trio is workable, but Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes and Fu (3D) would need to be weighed, and Zhang's death in 2018 limits his eligibility.
assessment.maturity: Independent experimental confirmations in HgTe, Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 have been robust since 2007-2009, and the field is mature. Haldane-related recognition in 2016 partly covers the neighbouring topology, which affects timeliness.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize leaves room for a second topology prize.
Allocation between Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the 3D theory of Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials. It is a clear case of prediction meeting experiment, with a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group did the experimental discovery. The configuration is neat. Cao and Fu in the experimental papers and others in the field, such as Kim, Dean and Yazdani for related experiments, may complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: The results are reproduced by many groups, but understanding of the superconducting mechanism is unsettled. It is a fast-developing field and arguably still young for a prize.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not understood.
Credit for early experimental work on twisted bilayers by others, and for the student-led first experiments, is not captured.
Timing may be premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering gave a standard ruler that independently confirms the dark-energy-dominated universe. As someone working on the dark-energy question, I find it an important clue from nature. It is, however, a confirmation of an existing picture rather than a surprise.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS) and Cole (2dFGRS) delivered the 2005 detections, and Sunyaev with Zeldovich laid the theoretical basis of acoustic oscillations. Colless could equally be argued for 2dFGRS, so the choice of three from four names is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: The result has been confirmed repeatedly by SDSS, BOSS, DESI and others. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy keep it topical but also leave the interpretation open.
uncertainties: The 2011 prize on cosmic acceleration already covers part of the same story.
Priority between theory and survey measurements is complicated.
DESI results could change the interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure provide an explanation for flatness, horizon uniformity and the seeds of galaxies, and the predicted spectrum of fluctuations matches CMB data. Its originality and influence are very large. As a sceptic of unconfirmed theory, I note that inflation itself has no direct evidence beyond the near-scale-invariant spectrum.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Starobinsky and Linde proposed inflation in different forms, and Mukhanov and Chibisov computed the fluctuations. Four names are credited, so a prize has to omit one or more, and the choice of Guth, Starobinsky and Mukhanov leaves out Linde, which is a hard allocation that I flag openly.
assessment.maturity: CMB observations support the broad picture, but primordial gravitational waves remain undetected and alternative explanations are not excluded. The idea may be mature enough yet still a theory awaiting a decisive test.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes yet, so the key distinguishing prediction is untested.
Linde is excluded in this configuration and the priority dispute between Starobinsky and Guth is unresolved.
My own work on trans-Planckian effects in inflation is a possible bias, since I take the physics seriously but doubt its status as established.
